card: This pull request fixes status bitmask checks and edge cases in block data availability queries. Previously, CheckBlockDataAvailability checked whether an upper block had any requested bit instead of all of them, which could cause a node to abort on an assertion inside GetFirstBlock when querying multi-bit masks. It also resolves bugs in the genesis block undo data exemption that caused valid undo queries to fail, missing block data to be masked, or single-block genesis ranges to be mishandled. The fix ensures callers like indexers accurately query availability without risking crash assertions.
changed_since_previous: No functional changes to the proposed solution; patch details and unit tests are now provided.
evidence: PR description: "CheckBlockDataAvailability checks whether the upper block has any requested bit. GetFirstBlock requires every requested bit, so a partial match can reach its assertion."
src/node/blockstorage.cpp diff: replaced `!(upper_block.nStatus & block_status)` with full mask checks on `upper_block` and `lower_block`, and updated `assert` in `GetFirstBlock` to `Assert`.
problem: In `CheckBlockDataAvailability`, testing the upper block with a bitwise AND (`upper_block.nStatus & block_status`) allowed partial bit matches to pass into `GetFirstBlock`, which asserts that all requested bits are present (`(last_block->nStatus & status_mask) == status_mask`). Furthermore, the genesis undo exception could reject valid undo-only requests down to genesis, accept blocks lacking block data if other requested flags matched, and mishandle single-block genesis queries.

risk.why: A logic error in block data availability checks could cause indexers or sync routines to misidentify pruned or missing blocks as present, or vice-versa.

summary: Fixes edge cases and assertion failures in `BlockManager::CheckBlockDataAvailability` by requiring all requested status bits rather than any bit before calling `GetFirstBlock`. It also refactors the genesis block undo data exemption to correctly handle undo-only requests, prevent non-undo flags from bypassing missing data checks, and support single-block ranges at genesis.
